title: is your ssn a secret trust account? the strawman theory EXPLAINED
summary: Debt-discharge seller explains the strawman and secret SSN trust theory, doubts the trust but promotes signature-as-credit and tender-of-payment tactics.

assertions.quote: the fact that your birth certificate is indeed a financial instrument

verdicts.note: The court sets out the theory that citizens are pledged as security for the national debt and rejects it as revisionist history and conspiracy theory; the authorities cited only concern leaving the gold standard.

assertions.quote: So that essentially confirms that your all caps name is a commercial entity.
So essentially this paved the way for a credit based currency because there was no gold.
So in 1933 the government declared bankruptcy and shifted from gold to credit.

verdicts.note: The federal government has never filed for or been placed in bankruptcy; it has kept borrowing, taxing and paying debts.

assertions.quote: understanding that you are the creditor and that your signature holds value
So if you do this, you file a tender of payment, okay, and they didn't re and they refuse it, then there's discharge

verdicts.note: UCC 3-603 discharge needs a real tender of money; self-made instruments are worthless and their use has been prosecuted as fraud.
The court rejected the argument that a bill of exchange not returned within 72 hours counts as honored; the case cited says nothing of the kind and the debt was not discharged.
Scotland's Court of Session rejected that a promissory note is full payment of a debt, adopted in Canadian courts; Rooke ACJ called it a 'conga line of promissory notes'.
The Tax Court (Goff) held a bonded promissory note presented to the IRS did not pay the taxpayer's liability, let collection proceed and imposed a $15,000 penalty; IRS-as-creditor only.

assertions.quote: If somebody ignores your present, you know you already won.

verdicts.note: Silence does not create a contract or discharge a debt; courts reject 'tacit acquiescence' affidavits.
No UCC provision makes failure to answer an 'Affidavit of Truth' within ten days an admission; a party cannot create a duty to respond by declaring one in a notarized document.
Foisted unilateral agreements (Three/Five Letters, 'tacit procuration') are pseudolaw; Rothweiler v Payette held the scheme so notoriously false that using it presumptively shows an abusive purpose.
No case has held that the IRS's failure to respond to a taxpayer's inquiry relieved the taxpayer of the duty to pay; IRS-as-creditor only.
The Three/Five Letters scheme rests on the misconception that a contract offer may be accepted by silence, analysed and rejected in Bank of Montreal v Rogozinsky.
Courts hold the Three/Five Letters scheme, where silence to notices supposedly makes a binding agreement, so notoriously false that using it implies abusive intent.
